name: Eiscir Riada

attributes.attribute: a band of eskers running from Dublin to Galway
the Irish word for a chain of low ridges, root of esker
the hill where the four provinces of Ireland meet

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Eiscir Riada is a site of Irish myth. The word eiscir means a chain of low ridges. That word grew into esker, the known term for a relic of ice. Ireland shook off its glaciers late. Until about ten thousand years ago, most of the island lay under ice. A band of eskers now runs from Dublin to Galway. It cuts the land almost in half. In old tales it marks the border between two kings. The king of the south may be Éremón or Eógan Mór. The king of the north may be Éber Finn or Conn of the Hundred Battles. Long ago the ridge served as a road across the bog. It crosses the Shannon near Uisneach, the heart where the four provinces meet.

okr.objective: Describe the Eiscir Riada as a glacial ridge that forms a mythic border in Ireland.
key_results: The word eiscir became the English term esker.
The band runs from Dublin to Galway and splits the island in two.
Scholars mark it as the border between the southern king Éremón and the king of the north, Éber.
It crossed the Shannon near Uisneach, the heart of the four provinces.
